purpose: Central registry for gameplay art requirements, existing assets, placeholders, and future art generation targets.

status_values.implemented: Used by current scenes, scripts, or configs.
status_values.available: Asset exists but is not wired into gameplay yet.
status_values.placeholder: Current gameplay uses a temporary or semantically imperfect asset.
status_values.missing: Required by design but no suitable asset is registered yet.

notes: Gameplay code should reference stable asset ids through this registry or domain configs.
Collision belongs to gameplay nodes, not to bitmap files.
Missing assets should use placeholders until the user explicitly asks for art generation.
Customer/random/civilian NPC walk sheets use 4 rows x 6 columns, 48x64 cells, and no duplicated standing endpoints.

Customer purchase profiles read crop preference items, demographic base budget/preferences, and personal random ranges from res://configs/customer_preferences.json, then blend demographic and per-NPC values 50/50.
Stall influence radius is configured per upgrade level in res://configs/upgrades.json and drives both customer InfluenceArea and chengguan InspectionTarget in scripts/world/stall.gd.

StallSpot StaticBody2D collision is a runtime open-stall blocker: scripts/world/stall_spot.gd keeps the template size/offset relative to Stall, disables it before opening, and enables/repositions it after a stall opens.

Town building nodes use an Area2D root with Visual and EndpointMarker children; CollisionShape2D is reserved for interaction/trigger area, while child StaticBody2D/CollisionShape2D is reserved for solid player/NPC collision.
Functional buildings such as SeedShop should keep the building root as res://scenes/npc_endpoint.tscn and compose gameplay behavior through child interaction components such as ShopInteraction.
New-game initialization should use PrototypeConstants.INITIAL_CASH for starting money; current baseline is 10 yuan.

Population flow uses statistical building population pools plus a probability transition matrix: configs/population.json, configs/flow_preferences.json, and configs/calendar.json feed PopulationFlow; PopulationFlowSpawner samples visible NPCs without instantiating the full town population.

Student and worker commute should be represented by PopulationFlow preferences rather than dedicated commute spawners; visible NPCs from a 10-minute flow tick should be queued and randomly spread across the next 10 game minutes.

PopulationFlow starts from Main with a detached TownScene template, keeps recent statistical flow events while the player is outside town, and PopulationFlowSpawner restores visible NPCs at route-progress positions when TownScene loads.

PopulationFlow background initialization must process the current aligned tick immediately when GameState.current_game_minute is already at or after the 06:00 day start, including load-game paths; it must not wait until the next 10-minute interval.

PopulationFlow target timing should stay generic: configs/flow_preferences.json time_curves adjusts attraction for age_group + target_type over the day, instead of adding hard-coded commute plans for specific buildings.

Population endpoint collection must only include nodes with the endpoint interface or a real endpoint_id property; generic Node2D children such as Visual, EndpointMarker, and collision nodes must never participate in population pools.
Customer overhead dialogue is probabilistic per event and must be based on an in-stock stall item the customer actually wants; avoid fixed dialogue triggers and stale sold-out item names.
Large raster maps should use a hybrid setup: Sprite2D background chunks for visuals plus separate gameplay nodes/layers for exits, collision, navigation, and interaction semantics.

Baked-map pixel occlusion can use Polygon2D with scripts/world/polygon_texture_occluder.gd: the polygon samples a configured map/background Sprite2D texture, such as TownScene/MapLayers/Sprite2D, with matching UVs and renders above the player, while collision remains separate StaticBody2D geometry.

CameraBounds uses a StaticBody2D root with a non-player collision layer as editable rectangle data for camera limits; TownScene also enables create_boundary_walls on CameraBounds instead of maintaining separate top/left/right/bottom Wall nodes.
